name: inquiry-goal-holdout
role: HOLDOUT — labelled before any v3 model call, evaluated ONCE. It is not a DEV set and must never be used to choose a prompt, a threshold or a contract. After its one sitting it is spent, exactly as the 67-case DEV set is.
question: Does merging DECISION into ANSWER raise the rate at which an ambiguous ANSWER request leaks to ACTION?
location: durable private eval store (~/.cache/sellerops-eval/inquiry-goal-holdout/v1) — messages and labels are never committed; this repository holds the build/check script, the schema, hashes and counts

sampling.snapshot: sellerops_f5_eval (the same clone the DEV corpus was drawn from)
sampling.after_seller_disposition: 291 ACTIVE (the seller has already marked 3,199 EXCLUDED_SPAM and 45 EXCLUDED_THREAD_REPLY)
sampling.after_contamination_rules: 190 distinct unused messages, then 89 after refusing placeholder bodies, quoted threads, seller-authored replies, operator connectivity tests and bench fixtures
sampling.note: Judgment-shaped messages are 7 of the 89 clean real candidates. The critical stratum is therefore ENRICHED roughly tenfold, on purpose: the absolute leak rate this set produces is NOT a production rate, and only the v2-vs-v3 difference is reported as a finding.

bench_fixtures_stored_as_REAL.why_it_matters: data_origin='REAL' does not distinguish them, and they are the cleanest judgment-shaped Korean in the pool — precisely the rows a holdout for this question would have reached for first. Refused by rule in build.py; not modified in the snapshot.

label_policy.author: designer, before any v3 model call
label_policy.space: the v3 three-token contract (ANSWER / STATE_READ / ACTION). A v2 arm is read into this space by folding its predictions; the gold is never folded the other way.
label_policy.HIGH: a careful reader lands on this label without argument
label_policy.MEDIUM: the label is defensible and the other reading is not absurd
label_policy.primary_metric_uses: HIGH only. MEDIUM is reported beside it and never folded in.
label_policy.minimal_pairs: every `pair` appears on BOTH sides of the gold, so a contract cannot score well by mapping the ambiguity marker to a token

evaluation.design: two arms, same 75 cases, one sitting: customer-goal-interpreter/v2 (four tokens) and /v3 (three). Paired, because the question is comparative and the DEV set can no longer answer it.
evaluation.primary: ACTION leakage on ANSWER-gold cases: predicted outcome ACTION where gold is ANSWER, over HIGH-confidence ANSWER-gold cases (n=26). The v2 arm's INFORMATION and DECISION fold to ANSWER before comparison.
evaluation.test: McNemar exact on the paired per-case leak indicator. b = v2 clean and v3 leaked; c = v2 leaked and v3 clean.

decision_rule.inconclusive: b > c and exact p >= 0.05 — reported as not distinguishable at this size; the merge ships only if b - c <= 2, otherwise HOLD
decision_rule.increase: b > c and exact p < 0.05 — the merge does not ship as it stands

evaluation.power: with 26 HIGH ANSWER-gold cases this set can detect roughly a tripling of the leak rate, not a doubling. Stated before the run so the result cannot be read as more than it is.
guards_that_must_not_regress: reverse leakage: ACTION-gold predicted ANSWER (stratum T, n=20 cases)
NO_GOAL violations on the 9 no-goal cases
evidence verbatim failures = 0 — a parse failure is a run failure, not a score
referent and constraint accuracy, which should be arm-invariant; movement there means something other than the token changed
evaluation.not_a_metric: overall outcome accuracy. The two arms have different label spaces, and the question is not accuracy.

spent_after: one sitting. A second use makes this a selection set, and the number it produced stops meaning what it said.
